source.title: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context
source.authors: Arnuv Tandon; Karan Dalal; Xinhao Li; Daniel Koceja; Marcel Rød; Sam Buchanan; Xiaolong Wang; J. Leskovec; O. Koyejo; Tatsunori B. Hashimoto; Carlos Guestrin; Jed McCaleb; Yejin Choi; Yu Sun

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether two modified Transformer architectures change loss at a matched parameter count, and also reports comparative loss trends over model-size and token-count sweeps. It does not fit the power laws or compute-optimal allocations in the claim.
record.gate_note: The training-compute sweeps report loss differences relative to full attention, not absolute loss scaling or fitted power laws; these results are recorded under fits_no_version. The study also reports held-out loss comparisons for modified architectures without TTT, which bear on V4.
record.test_reason: This is a long-context test-time-training methods paper, not a scaling-law study. Its only result bearing on a version is an incidental ablation in Section 3.2. With TTT switched off (b = 8K), the modified, parameter-matched TTT-E2E architecture (smaller MLP hidden dimensions plus a second MLP in the last 1/4 of blocks) reaches 2.825 against 2.827 for full attention at 760M on DCLM. That is a narrow test of V4 in a new setting. The compute sweeps (Figure 5) plot only loss differences from full attention, with no absolute loss and no power-law fit, so they bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase misses the paper's headline. The authors' main conclusion is that TTT-E2E, a sliding-window Transformer that keeps training on its context at test time, matches full attention's scaling with context length at 3B/164B tokens, unlike Mamba 2 and Gated DeltaNet. It also has constant inference latency, 2.7× faster than full attention at 128K, but is worse at needle-in-a-haystack recall and slower to train at short context. The compute-scaling result, that it follows full attention's trend under larger budgets, is a secondary claim. The tokenizer and data effects are explicitly anecdotal.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares relative loss differences for TTT-E2E and baselines across model-size and token-count sweeps; it does not fit scaling-law exponents or find compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported relative loss trends vary with training budget, tokenizer, and dataset. The authors identify roughly 760M as the model-size regime boundary and roughly 48B tokens as the token-count boundary.

fits_no_version.finding: TTT-E2E's loss advantage over full attention shrinks with compute below about 760M parameters and about 48B tokens, then stays roughly flat. The authors note the trend varied anecdotally with tokenizer and dataset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative loss gaps between sequence architectures change with training budget, then stabilise beyond a compute threshold.

record.problems: The compute-scaling results are primarily plotted as differences from full attention rather than absolute loss; no scaling exponents or predictive fits are reported. The tokenizer and dataset sensitivity findings are described as anecdotal.

untested.parts: No absolute held-out loss is plotted against parameters, tokens or compute, and no power-law form is fitted.
The token budget uses the Chinchilla ratio as an input; no compute-optimal allocation is measured.
Depth, width, aspect ratio and other shape choices across a wide range and across sizes are not tested; the only evidence is one MLP-structure change at 760M.
NIAH is reported only for a cross-method comparison at 3B, not as a function of scale.
No exponents are fitted; tokenizer and data effects are shown only on relative advantage.

missing.what: Adding QK norm to Gated DeltaNet at 760M, a small architecture detail, changes loss from 2.814 to 2.809 in pre-training at 8K and from 2.691 to 2.683 at 32K fine-tuning. This is a minor V4-relevant architecture-detail effect, but parameter matching is not stated.

record.verdict_notes: The connection to the scaling-law claim is weak. The study is chiefly T4-like, with its own method compared against baselines, and the V4 support rests on a single ablation at one scale. The rows' cited figure locator is Section 3.2, 'Modified architectures without TTT' (values given in text). The Figure 5 relative-Δ sweeps cannot speak to V1 or V3 because absolute losses are never reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether absolute held-out loss follows a power law in parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run power-law fits are used to predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or parameter/token growth exponents are reported.
The comparison covers two modified architectures without TTT at one setup, not a wide range of depth, width, and architecture designs.
The experiments are language-modeling experiments; other modalities and the listed training regimes are not tested.
The study does not test downstream-task performance as a predictable function of scale or pretraining loss.
The study reports sensitivity of relative loss advantages to tokenizer and data, and compute-regime trends, but does not test fitted exponents, fitting choices, or compute-optimal allocations.

rows.subject: TTT-E2E (modified architecture without TTT)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated the modified architecture without TTT against full attention.
rows.note: The authors describe the loss as almost no different from full attention; the architecture is parameter-matched by reducing MLP hidden dimensions.
rows.check: Valid as a narrow V4 test. The paper states parameter matching explicitly for TTT-E2E: hidden dimensions are reduced so total parameters stay the same. The architecture change is MLP width and splitting into two MLPs in some blocks, not depth or width in general.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2, modified architectures without TTT; Section 2.3.1, two MLP layers per block.

rows.subject: TTT-KVB (modified architecture without TTT)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated the modified architecture without TTT against full attention.
rows.note: The authors describe the loss as almost no different from full attention; the architecture is parameter-matched by reducing MLP hidden dimensions.
rows.check: The note claims TTT-KVB is parameter-matched by reducing MLP hidden dimensions. The paper states that only for TTT-E2E. TTT-KVB adds outer-loop θK/θV and multi-head LoRA MLPs, and its parameter count is not reported. The fixed-parameter-count condition of V4 is therefore unverified for this row.

source_check.correct: TTT-KVB without TTT has loss 2.826 versus full attention's 2.827 in the nominal 760M ablation on DCLM at 8K context with b = 8K. Parameter matching by reducing MLP hidden dimensions is explicitly stated for TTT-E2E only; remove that assertion from the TTT-KVB note.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2, modified architectures without TTT; Section 2.3.1, parameter matching for TTT-E2E; Section 2.4.2, TTT-KVB architecture differences.
source_check.problem: The note incorrectly extends TTT-E2E's explicit parameter-matching procedure to TTT-KVB.

rows.subject: TTT-E2E (model-size sweep)
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss difference from full attention across model sizes.

conditions.value: model size; small-budget regime below roughly 760M and medium-budget regime above it

rows.note: The authors say TTT-E2E's advantage over full attention decreases as compute increases in the small-budget regime; in the medium-budget regime it follows a similar trend, with a small uptick. This is a relative-loss trend, not an absolute-loss power-law fit.
rows.check: Relative loss Δ versus full attention only; no absolute loss or fit. Correctly unlinked.

rows.subject: TTT-E2E (model-size sweep)
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss difference from full attention across model sizes.

conditions.value: model size; small-budget regime below roughly 760M and medium-budget regime above it

rows.note: The authors describe the same broad trend across panels: the relative advantage decreases with more compute in the small-budget regime and is similar to full attention in the medium-budget regime. This is a relative-loss trend, not an absolute-loss power-law fit.

rows.subject: TTT-E2E (760M model; token-count sweep)
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss difference from full attention across pretraining token counts.
rows.note: The authors say the relative advantage decreases with more compute in the small-budget regime and that TTT-E2E follows a similar trend to full attention in the medium-budget regime. This is not an absolute-loss power-law fit.

rows.subject: TTT-E2E (760M model; token-count sweep)
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss difference from full attention across fine-tuning token counts.
rows.note: The authors describe the same broad trend across panels. This is a relative-loss trend, not an absolute-loss power-law fit.
rows.check: As for R3. The sweep covers fine-tuning tokens at 5% of pre-training tokens, not 16B–80B fine-tuning tokens as such; the x-axis label is ambiguous.

rows.subject: TTT-E2E (3B model)
rows.operation_detail: Compared the relative advantage over full attention after changing tokenizer.
rows.locator: Section 3.3, Sensitivity to tokenizer and data quality
rows.note: The report calls this an anecdotal observation.
rows.check: Anecdotal change in the method's advantage over a baseline. This compares the study's own method against others, so it should not be read as a claim result.

rows.subject: TTT-E2E (760M model; token-count sweep)
rows.operation_detail: Compared relative loss trends under different training datasets.
rows.measure: Trend in loss difference from full attention
rows.value: DCLM and FineWebEdu showed the same trend as full attention after 48B tokens; SlimPajama showed a small uptick
rows.locator: Section 3.3, Sensitivity to tokenizer and data quality
rows.note: The authors describe this as anecdotal and say a comprehensive investigation is beyond the paper's scope.
rows.check: Anecdotal relative-trend comparison of the study's own method against full attention; it bears on no version. The baseline field is muddled: SlimPajama is the contrast, not DCLM and FineWebEdu.

relationships.condition: 760M models pre-trained on DCLM at 8K context, TTT disabled (b = 8K), parameter-matched MLP restructuring (TTT-E2E architecture)
relationships.reason: The modified architecture reaches loss 2.825 against 2.827 for full attention, which the authors call almost no different (R1). TTT-KVB gives 2.826, but its parameter match is unstated (R2).
relationships.display_finding: The restructured architecture reached loss 2.825 versus 2.827 for full attention; TTT-KVB reached 2.826, although its parameter match was unspecified.

relation.reason: The parameter-matched architecture ablation directly bears on V4, even though scaling-law estimation is not the paper's main question.

tranche.reason: The methods paper supplies an incidental architecture-insensitivity result in a new setting, rather than a different method aimed at establishing scaling laws.

source_check.notes: Support for V4 is local to the tested architecture comparison; a wide range of shapes remains untested. Negligible loss change is consistent with observing V4's architecture insensitivity.
